previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol dependence, alcoholic cirrhosis, portal hypertension, esophageal varices, and asthma was admitted for abdominal pain and alcohol withdrawal following a relapse involving daily consumption of brandy. He presented with epigastric and right upper quadrant pain radiating to the back, tremulousness, and anxiety. He was managed with CIWA-guided diazepam tapering, restarted on home medications including nadolol, spironolactone, omeprazole, and lactulose, and treated for pain with acetaminophen, tramadol, and hydromorphone. His withdrawal symptoms resolved, liver enzymes improved, and abdominal pain decreased during the hospitalization. Social work engaged him in counseling, and plans were made to restart Suboxone and follow up with primary care and addiction services. He was discharged home in stable condition with clear instructions on abstinence, medication adherence, and follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with PMH of alcoholic 
pancreatitis, ETOH abuse, hepatitis, and cirrhosis presents with 
one week history of worsening epigastric abdominal pain 
associated with nausea and non-bloody emesis concerning for 
alcoholic hepatitis.

# Abdominal Pain/EtOH pancreaticohepatitis: Pt with symptoms 
concerning for alcoholic hepatitis vs chronic pancreatitis. He 
does not have an elevated lipase, mild transaminitis, and 
elevated TBili and ALP which are not far off baseline (ALP 
400-600 and TBili ___ but consistent with cholestatic 
process. RUQ did not show cholelithiasis or cholecystitis. This 
is likely alcoholic hepatitis/cirrhosis vs chronic pancreatitis 
in setting of recent ETOH consumption. His pain was controlled 
with IV Dilaudid with transition to PO Dilaudid. His diet was 
ADAT and he was given IVF until he was tolerating PO. 

# Alcohol Dependence/Withdrawal: In ED had an ETOH level of 401 
indicating recent consumption PTA. Also with AG metabolic 
acidosis likely from ETOH. He has a history of withdrawal on 
prior admissions where he experienced tactile hallucinations, 
anxiety, and tremulousness. He has history of withdrawal 
seizures. He was monitored with CIWA and given Ativan as needed. 
At time of discharge, he was requiring minimal Ativan 
requirements. 

# Presumed EtOH Cirrhosis: ETOH cirrhosis complicated by portal 
hypertension and varices. RUQ US showed coarse nodular liver 
with splenomegaly and hepatopetal flow in the main portal vein 
suggestive of cirrhosis. No encephalopathy, ascites, or 
asterixis. He was continued on Nadolol 20 mg PO DAILY for 
esophageal varices, Spironolactone 50 mg PO DAILY, Omeprazole 40 
mg PO DAILY. Lactulose 30 mL PO DAILY given abdominal pain was 
held but restarted on discharge. 

# Hypernatremia: Pt with Na 146 on admission, likely from GI 
losses from vomiting. Improved with D5W. Normal on discharge. 

# Asthma: Pt with wheezing on exam and may have mild 
exacerbation. Recently was treated with oral steroids. Treated 
with 5 day course of PO prednisone. On discharge, his lungs were 
clear, without wheeze. His shortness of breath had improved and 
he was ambulating without difficulty.

patent, but demonstrates hepatofugal flow, unchanged from prior study.  The
gallbladder is unremarkable without stones, wall thickening or pericholecystic
fluid.  The spleen is again enlarged measuring 14.5 cm.  There is no ascites.

main portal vein and splenomegaly, suggestive of cirrhosis with portal
hypertension.
